headline: The bounce narrowed to five tickers while the long end re-broke: NDX +1.2% with equal-weight -0.7%, 10y back to 5.15%, and leveraged loans at a new low (BKLN z=-1.36).
summary: Yesterday the story was hedges that wouldn't come off. Today they came off — and the tape got worse underneath. VIX fell another 7.8% to 18.44, SKEW dropped 4.0% off its 52-week high to 161.86, VIX/VIX3M backed away from inversion to 0.941. Spot vol is now cheap-ish and the panic premium is gone. But the rally that paid for it was the narrowest kind: NDX +1.2%, SOXX +1.7%, SMH +1.6%, AMZN +5.0%, PLTR +4.4%, MU +3.0%, TSLA +3.8%, XBI +2.5% — against equal-weight RSP/SPY -0.7%, SPW -0.3%, DJI -0.1%, XLF -0.8%, JPM -1.8%, IAI -1.3%, XLU -2.0%, XLRE -1.2%. SPX closed +0.4% on a day most of it fell. IWM/SPY sits at z=-1.37 and the 6.6th percentile of its year. That is a squeeze in the most-shorted momentum names, not a broadening.

Rates did the opposite of last week and that is the binding constraint again. 10y +6bp to 5.15%, 30y +5bp to 5.48%, 5y +5bp to 4.94%, and the 10y real yield +6bp to 2.80% — 28.4% above its 200-day, +87bp year-to-date. TLT -0.7%, IEF -0.4%, MOVE 101.3 and +25.6% on the month. The rates composite deteriorated to -58 from -56. 2s10s steepened 3bp to 38bp with acceleration z=1.45 — the long end is leading, which is the bad kind of steepening. The clearing price is unchanged and unanswered: the 30-year mortgage is 7.40%, +64bp in a month, z=1.91, 100th percentile. ITB -1.7% and DHI -2.9% on an up day for the index; XHB/SPY is at the 3.8th percentile of its 52-week range and 15.8% below its 200-day. No part of yesterday's equity repair touched housing.

Credit refused to participate and made the day's genuine new low. BKLN -0.6% to 20.32, z=-1.36 with acceleration z=-1.20 — leveraged loans are now the weakest z-score on the tape outside Korea. HYG flat at 76.83 but z=-1.14 and -1.7% on the month; LQD -0.5% at the 17.5th percentile. Loans selling off while VIX falls 7.8% and SPX rises is the cleanest divergence available. Second liquidation: precious metals. Gold -0.6% to 4,157 (z=-1.50, -6.1% on the month, 14.5th percentile), silver -14.2% on the month at z=-1.64, platinum -8.7%, GDXJ -12.9%, and gold/silver +9.5% on the month with acceleration z=1.42. Third: anything levered to the AI-power buildout keeps dying — REMX -22.7% on the month and 37.3% below its 200-day at the 0th percentile, NLR -13.4% (0th), URA -15.3% (0th), GRID -5.1%, CEG -3.0%, VST -1.5%, GEV -1.4%.

What genuinely improved: the inflation tax and the Asia funding scare. WTI -3.1% to 98.28, RBOB -4.3% today and -12.3% on the month (z=-1.22), corn -11.5%, wheat -8.2%. Copper +0.7% to 6.576 at the 88th percentile, copper/gold +1.3% at the 94.5th, AUDUSD +0.9% and AUDJPY +1.1%. Korea bounced hard — EWY +4.1%, KOSPI +2.0% after a -15.6% month (z=-2.27) — with USDKRW -0.8% to 1,330.4, dead last in its 52-week range. That still reads as positioning unwound, not funding stress. LatAm is the only real relative-strength story left outside energy and healthcare: EWZ +11.8% on the month (z=1.31, rs +11.1% vs SPX), BVSP z=1.80, MXX +8.9% (z=1.91), with USDBRL -1.1% today. Defensive leadership hardened again — XLV +4.7% on the month with acceleration z=1.60, XLP acc z=1.89, WMT +11.2% (acc z=1.86), COST +11.2%, USMV at the 96.6th percentile. Energy equity still owns the top of the range on a day crude fell: XLE 98.3rd percentile, XOP 98.8th, XOM and CVX at 99th. Risk regime -19 versus -18 — the number barely moved, but the composition rotated from everyone hedging to nobody hedging and credit cracking.

good.text: The hedging panic deflated: VIX -7.8% to 18.44, SKEW -4.0% to 161.86 off its 52-week high, VIX/VIX3M back to 0.941 from the edge of inversion. Tail protection is cheaper than it was 48 hours ago.

The Asia semis unwind is reversing on no funding stress: EWY +4.1%, KOSPI +2.0% after a -15.6% month, SOXX +1.7%, SMH +1.6%, TSM +1.8%, MU +3.0% — with USDKRW at 1,330.4, the 0th percentile of its year.
The commodity inflation tax keeps draining: RBOB -4.3% today and -12.3% on the month (z=-1.22), WTI -3.1% to 98.28, corn -11.5%, wheat -8.2%. 5y breakeven only +1bp.
Cyclical FX and copper confirm no growth scare: copper +0.7% at the 88th percentile, copper/gold +1.3% at the 94.5th, AUDUSD +0.9%, AUDJPY +1.1%.
LatAm is the cleanest trend on the board: EWZ +11.8% and BVSP +10.7% on the month (z=1.80), MXX +8.9% (z=1.91, acc z=1.60), USDBRL -1.1% today and -8.0% YTD.
Defensive quality is accelerating, not fading: XLV +4.7% month with acc z=1.60, XLP acc z=1.89, WMT +11.2% (acc z=1.86), COST +11.2%, USMV at the 96.6th percentile.

bad.text: The long end re-broke after last week's rally: 10y +6bp to 5.15%, 30y 5.48%, 10y real yield 2.80% and 28.4% above its 200-day. MOVE 101.3, +25.6% on the month. Rates composite worsened to -58.
Leveraged loans made the day's new low while stocks rose and vol fell — BKLN z=-1.36 with acceleration z=-1.20, HYG z=-1.14, LQD at the 17.5th percentile. Credit is not confirming anything.
Breadth went the wrong way on an up day: RSP/SPY -0.7% against NDX +1.2%, IWM/SPY at the 6.6th percentile (z=-1.37), XLF -0.8%, JPM -1.8%, IAI -1.3%, KRE/SPY at the 22.5th.
Housing is the unresolved clearing price: 30-year mortgage 7.40%, +64bp on the month, z=1.91, 100th percentile. ITB -1.7%, DHI -2.9% into a green index; XHB/SPY at the 3.8th percentile.
Precious metals liquidation is accelerating, not stabilizing: gold z=-1.50 (-6.1% month), silver -14.2% month (z=-1.64), platinum -8.7%, GDXJ -12.9%, gold/silver acc z=1.42.
The AI-power complex keeps being sold outright: REMX -22.7% month and 37.3% below its 200-day (0th pct), NLR -13.4% (0th), URA -15.3% (0th), GRID -5.1%, CEG -3.0%, GEV -1.4%.

trades.name: 2s30s curve steepener
trades.expr: DV01-neutral long TU (2y) vs short WN/US (30y) futures; or buy TBT against a long position in 2y notes. Size to ~1bp of curve per unit.
trades.thesis: The long end is repricing term premium independently of the Fed path. 30y 5.48% and 10y real 2.80% sit 8.7% and 28.4% above their 200-days with MOVE +25.6% on the month — supply and inflation-risk premium, not growth. 2y is anchored (+1bp on the month, acc z=-1.55) while 10s and 30s are +14bp each.
trades.trigger: Today 10y +6bp, 30y +5bp, 2y only +3bp; 2s10s +3bp to 38bp with acceleration z=1.45 and the curve still only at the 33rd percentile of its year — plenty of room.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 25bp, or 30y yield below 5.25% on a bull-flattening growth scare.

trades.name: Short home construction (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB: mortgage 7.40%, 100th pctile, nothing priced
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan ITB 80 puts; pair against long XLV if you want sector-neutral.
trades.thesis: A 7.40% 30-year mortgage with the 10y back at 5.15% is a demand shutdown that homebuilder multiples have only half-discounted. Affordability is at the 100th percentile of restrictiveness and still accelerating (mortgage acc z=1.34).
trades.trigger: ITB -1.7% and DHI -2.9% on a day SPX closed +0.4%; the 10y gave back 6bp of last week's rally. XHB/SPY at the 3.8th percentile, ITB 11.3% below its 200-day.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back below 6.90%, or ITB closing above 92 (reclaiming its 200-day).

trades.name: Short high-yield credit via HYG puts
trades.line: Buy HYG puts: loans at z=-1.36 while VIX fell 7.8%
trades.expr: Buy Dec/Jan HYG 75 puts, funded by selling 79 calls; or short BKLN outright for the cleaner, less-hedged expression.
trades.thesis: Credit is the one market that refused to take the equity bounce. Loans — the most senior, most floating-rate part of the stack — are the weakest z-score on the tape, which says it is cash-flow coverage at 5%+ front-end rates, not duration. Equity vol is now cheap enough to hedge this asymmetrically.
trades.trigger: BKLN -0.6% to a new low at z=-1.36, acc z=-1.20, HYG -1.7% on the month at z=-1.14, LQD -0.5% at the 17.5th percentile — all on a day VIX fell 7.8% and SPX rose 0.4%.
trades.stop: BKLN reclaims 20.60 and HYG/IEF z back above zero.

trades.name: Long energy E&P (XOP) vs SPY
trades.line: Long XOP vs SPY: 98th pctile holding on down-crude days
trades.expr: Long XOP, short equal dollars of SPY. Add XOM/CVX as the lower-beta version.
trades.thesis: Energy equity is absorbing lower crude without giving back relative strength — the market is capitalizing a higher through-cycle Brent, not spot. Brent is still +5.2% on the month and +22.4% on three at 109.23.
trades.trigger: On a day WTI fell 3.1%, XLE held the 98.3rd percentile, XOP the 98.8th, XOM and CVX the 99th; XLE relative strength +5.4% 1m / +13.7% 3m and rising.
trades.stop: Brent below 98, or XOP/SPY relative strength turning down for two weeks.

trades.name: Long QUAL vs short SPHB
trades.line: Fade the beta squeeze: QUAL long, SPHB short
trades.expr: Long QUAL, short SPHB, equal dollar notional.
trades.thesis: Today's rally was a short-cover in the most levered, lowest-quality cohort while the broad tape fell. High beta/low vol is still in a month-long downtrend (z=-1.10, acc z=-1.03) and breadth is deteriorating — the regime favors balance-sheet quality, which is accelerating, not beta.
trades.trigger: SPHB/SPLV +2.1% today but z=-1.10; RSP/SPY -0.7% and IWM/SPY at the 6.6th percentile on the same day. QUAL at the 94th percentile, USMV 96.6th with acc z=1.13.
trades.stop: SPHB/SPLV above 2.05 with RSP/SPY turning up — a genuine broadening.

trades.name: Long Korea (EWY)
trades.line: Long EWY: -13.6% month, won at 0th pctile, now +4.1%
trades.expr: Long EWY; aggressive version adds TSM/EWT on weakness. Hedge index beta with a partial SPY short if desired.
trades.thesis: Korea's -15.6% monthly collapse (KOSPI z=-2.27) happened with the won at the strongest end of its 52-week range — a forced de-grossing of the semis trade, not a credit or funding event. That setup mean-reverts violently when the selling stops.
trades.trigger: EWY +4.1% and KOSPI +2.0% today with USDKRW -0.8% to 1,330.4 at the 0th percentile; SOXX +1.7%, MU +3.0%, TSM +1.8% confirming the complex.
trades.stop: USDKRW back above 1,370, or EWY closing below 148.

trades.name: Long Brazil (EWZ) vs EEM
trades.line: Long EWZ vs EEM: +11.8% month, real strengthening
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EEM equal dollar. Unhedged BRL is the point — don't currency-hedge this.
trades.thesis: Brazil is the only EM with equity momentum and currency strength together: real rates falling from a punitive level into a still-firm commodity complex. Broad EM is rolling over (EEM/SPY z=-1.49, acc z=-1.51), which makes the pair the efficient expression rather than outright EM beta.
trades.trigger: EWZ +11.8% and BVSP +10.7% on the month (z=1.80, relative strength +11.1% vs SPX, turning up) with USDBRL -1.1% today to 5.04 and -8.0% YTD.
trades.stop: USDBRL above 5.30, or EWZ relative strength vs EEM rolling over for three weeks.
